verbatims.quote: Beat the sportsbooks. Yeah, that one. That's the whole reason anybody bets. I don't really know what a line move is though.
Nobody beats the books with an odds screen. 'Bet like a pro' reads like every tout on Twitter selling a $99 Discord. Show me the numbers and skip the slogans.
Four books side by side is the part I'd actually use. But if the odds are hours old when I tap in, I'm deleting it.
Insiders sounds like inside info. If it's just the guys from TV, I can already watch TV.
Give me props and hit rates for my guys. I don't need another podcast host to follow.
Honestly I bet the Eagles and a parlay on Sundays. I'd open it to see my game and that's about it.
Refreshing a few times a day is honest, but it's the first thing a sharp will poke at. And 'every number you need' oversells it if the prop coverage is thin.
An AI that won't tell me what to bet? Then what's it for. I can read a stat page myself.

researcher_note: B and H (casual favorites) backfire with serious and industry respondents (below 2). F wins weekly and serious bettors but casuals rate it low because they don't know what it means. 'My teams' beats line moves ~2:1 for first screen; 56% would pay for nothing; some casuals read 'insiders' as inside information.
